core_obligations: Replace K and L by bounded complexes of finite free modules with comparison maps that are isomorphisms above the given degrees and surjections in those degrees (proof lines 16498-16505).
Form the tensor product of the two comparison maps and observe that it induces isomorphisms above the degree t = max(m+a, n+b) and a surjection in degree t (proof lines 16505-16512).
Deduce the two parts of the statement, using the pseudo-coherence criterion for the second (proof lines 16512-16514).
proof_roadmap: Choose the two bounded complexes with their comparison maps (proof lines 16498-16505).
Tensor the comparison maps and read off the cohomology behaviour (proof lines 16505-16512).
Conclude pseudo-coherence in both parts (proof lines 16512-16514).
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the pseudo-coherence of a derived tensor product of two bounded above complexes in terms of the two individual bounds, and the proof is a 17-line argument that replaces both complexes by bounded complexes of finite free modules with the prescribed cohomology comparison maps and then studies the tensor product of those maps. It observes that the tensor product of the two comparison maps induces isomorphisms above the expected degree and a surjection in that degree, and it closes by referring to the spectral sequence of tors for the verification and citing the pseudo-coherence criterion for the second part. The construction of the two comparison maps is displayed; the spectral sequence step is left to the reader.
